purpose: The single machine-readable record of the pinned toolchain, read by the doctor and bootstrap verbs of ./build.sh and ./build.ps1.

Authority: docs/technical/100-build-dependencies-and-release-operations.md § Toolchain pinning, which requires that a bootstrap command 'verifies/downloads approved public tools or prints exact manual installation instructions and checks hashes'.
Owned by the FND-002 integration owner. A tool is added here only with the dependency request recorded in doc 100 § Dependency policy.

dotnet_sdk.install_directory_reason: hostfxr's default probe path. Godot's GodotPlugins host resolves the runtime from there with no DOTNET_ROOT and no dotnet on PATH; a custom install directory breaks the headless game launch.

godot.unpinned_platform_policy: A platform with no recorded hash is reported by doctor as an explicit warning naming this file, never as a silent pass. Recording the Windows and macOS hashes is FND-002 follow-on work; doc 100 § Toolchain pinning requires the pin, and only linux-x64 has been bootstrapped so far.

godot_export_templates.deferred_reason: 1.2 GB. Needed only by the export and package verbs, whose owner is FND-006. doctor reports it as deferred until that package lands, and never fails on its absence.

optional_tools.name: blender
optional_tools.deferred_reason: doc 100 § Toolchain pinning requires the exact Blender major/minor/patch used by derivation scripts. No derivation script exists until AST-002, so the exact version is pinned by that package. doctor reports Blender as deferred, not missing.

optional_tools.name: pwsh
optional_tools.deferred_reason: build.ps1 is the Windows workflow wrapper. PowerShell is not required on Linux or macOS; when it is present, build/verify-wrapper-parity.sh proves wrapper parity by executing both wrappers instead of by comparing their sources.

optional_tools.name: xvfb-run
optional_tools.deferred_reason: --headless uses the dummy rendering driver and cannot capture a viewport, so the screenshot/render tier needs Xvfb plus a software Vulkan ICD. No screenshot verification exists until PRE-004.

required_commands_policy: An entry here is a command the workflow cannot function without, and doctor's job is to establish that BEFORE a gate runs. Presence on PATH is not the requirement; capability is. macOS ships a bash and a sed that are both present and both unable to do what the gate scripts need, and an earlier version of this list probed only git, unzip and curl - so doctor passed on a Mac where ./build.sh build then died in build/verify-gate-wiring.sh. A preflight that certifies an environment its own gates cannot run in is worse than no preflight, because it moves the reader's suspicion onto their own machine.

Capability is established by RUNNING the command (minimum_major_version, or capability_arguments whose exit status demonstrates it), never by inspecting the platform. A uname test would be wrong the moment someone installs gnu-sed or coreutils, which is the normal macOS remedy and therefore the case that matters most.

Two commands are deliberately NOT probed here. 'readlink -f' and 'sed -i' were requirements of build/verify-verbs.sh and build/verify-gate-wiring.sh respectively; both call sites were rewritten to portable forms in the same change that added this list, so probing for them would assert a requirement the repository no longer has. A probe for a dependency that has been removed is the same defect as a missing probe for one that exists: the list stops describing the workflow.

required_commands.name: git
required_commands.reason: source revision identity in verb results and evidence bundles

required_commands.name: unzip
required_commands.reason: bootstrap extracts the pinned Godot archive

required_commands.name: curl
required_commands.reason: bootstrap downloads the pinned Godot archive and the .NET install script

required_commands.name: bash
required_commands.reason: the gate scripts use the 'mapfile' builtin in 32 places, which arrived in bash 4.0; under Apple's bash 3.2 they abort mid-run with 'mapfile: command not found' rather than reporting a finding
required_commands.remedy: brew install bash, then put Homebrew's bin ahead of /bin on PATH: export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH". Every script under build/ is '#!/usr/bin/env bash', so PATH order is what selects the interpreter. build/gate-output.sh repeats this check for a gate invoked directly.

required_commands.name: sha256sum
required_commands.reason: build/verify-format.sh and build/verify-policies.sh hash fixtures and the deterministic assembly with it; macOS has 'shasum -a 256' instead and no sha256sum at all
required_commands.remedy: brew install coreutils, then export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" so the GNU names are the ones found

required_commands.name: timeout
required_commands.reason: build/verify-godot-runner.sh bounds a hanging engine run with 'timeout --kill-after'; stock macOS has no timeout command at all, so a hang there would run without a bound
required_commands.remedy: brew install coreutils, then export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" so the GNU names are the ones found

required_commands.name: sed
required_commands.reason: the strip_ansi function in build/verify-godot.sh strips ANSI from engine logs with the \x1b escape, which is a GNU sed extension. BSD sed does not fail on it, it matches a literal 'x1b' - so the engine log is silently left unstripped and the ERROR-line assertions read colour codes as content. A wrong answer rather than an error is why this is probed rather than left to chance
required_commands.capability_description: GNU sed (BSD sed has no --version and no \xHH escape)
required_commands.remedy: brew install gnu-sed, then export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/opt/gnu-sed/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" so 'sed' is the GNU one
